newsitem.title: UK: British Steel eases as Merrill downgrades.
newsitem.headline: British Steel eases as Merrill downgrades.

text.p: Shares in British Steel Plc eased 4-1/2p to 155 in active trading on Tuesday as Merrill Lynch downgraded its rating and halved its 1997-98 earnings estimates.
Brokerage HSBC James Capel also downgraded the stock.
Both brokerages linked the downgrades to the sharp appreciation of sterling, which rose to a 4-1/2 year high against the German mark.
A strong currency hurts profits of companies that do a large proportion of their business overseas.

Merrill Lynch engineering analyst Paul Compton said he cut his rating on the stock to "reduce" from "neutral," and slashed his earnings estimates to 140 million stg from 280 million stg for the 1997-98 fiscal year.

Capel downgraded the stock to "hold" from "buy," and cut its profit forecast for the current fiscal year to 470 million stg from 500 million stg, market sources. Capel also reduced its forecasts for the 1997-98 and 1998-99 fiscal years to 200 million stg from 320 million stg, and to 457 million stg from 577 million stg, respectively.
